report.answer_text:
In 2025, Google's main Willow report was a claim of "verifiable quantum advantage" on October 22.
The claim: Google's 105-qubit Willow processor was used to demonstrate a "verifiable quantum advantage."[1] The algorithm is called Quantum Echoes. It uses out-of-time-order correlators (OTOCs), which work like quantum "echo" signals, to probe chaotic dynamics on a 65-qubit subsystem of the chip.[1]
Speed: Google said it ran 13,000 times faster than the world's best supercomputer could manage.[2] One write-up says certain data points would take an estimated 3+ years each to simulate on Frontier, while the quantum chip produced them in seconds.[1]
Verifiability: The results were published in *Nature*. Google says the algorithm is verifiable, meaning another quantum computer can repeat it.[2]
Applications: Google said the result clears a path for useful applications within five years.[2] It pointed to possible uses in medicine and materials science.[2]
Context: The Willow chip itself is older than these results. Google launched it in December 2024.[3] That launch centered on error correction. Google said errors fall exponentially as the chip scales up.[4] It described this as cracking a key challenge the field had pursued for almost 30 years.[4]
The advantage claim comes from Google. HPCwire's coverage put it conditionally: "If it pans out," it would be the first time a quantum computer has achieved quantum advantage.[3] Independent scrutiny and the practical usefulness of the task are still open questions.
